banner.title: Cookies and your data
banner.description: We use strictly necessary cookies to keep you signed in and to remember your language. With your consent we also measure anonymous usage. You can refuse, and change your mind at any time.

prefs.title: Cookie preferences
prefs.description: Choose which categories you allow. Strictly necessary storage cannot be switched off — the site does not work without it. Nothing else runs until you allow it.
prefs.necessaryDescription: Your sign-in session, your interface language, and the record of this choice. Exempt from consent under the ePrivacy Directive.
prefs.analyticsDescription: Anonymous usage measurement (Vercel Analytics) — which pages are opened and how often. No advertising, no profiling, no sale of data.
prefs.policyLink: Read the full cookie and privacy notice

policy.title: Cookie and privacy notice
policy.intro: This notice explains what SandStats stores in your browser, why, and what you can decide about it. It is written to meet the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the ePrivacy Directive.
policy.controllerBody: The controller for this processing is the operator of SandStats. For any question about your data, or to exercise the rights below, write to {{contact}}.
policy.sessionPurpose: Keeps you signed in after you log in. Set by the SandStats API and not readable by scripts.
policy.languagePurpose: Remembers the interface language you picked.
policy.consentPurpose: Stores the choice you made here so you are not asked again on every page. Kept in localStorage.
policy.consentRetention: 12 months, then you are asked again
policy.analyticsPurpose: Counts page views to show which parts of the site are used. Loaded only after you allow it.
policy.basisNecessary: Strictly necessary storage runs on legitimate interest (art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) and, where it serves a feature you asked for, on the contract with you (art. 6(1)(b)). It is exempt from the consent requirement of art. 5(3) of the ePrivacy Directive.
policy.basisAnalytics: Analytics runs only on your consent (art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). Refusing costs you nothing — every feature of the site works the same either way.
policy.recipientsBody: Anonymous usage measurement is provided by Vercel Inc. acting as a processor. No data is sold, no advertising network is used and no profiles are built. Where data is transferred outside the EEA it relies on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.
policy.rightsIntro: Under the GDPR you have the following rights over your personal data:
policy.rightAccess: Access — obtain a copy of the data held about you (art. 15).
policy.rightRestriction: Restriction — limit how your data is used (art. 18).
policy.rightPortability: Portability — receive your data in a machine-readable format (art. 20).
policy.rightObject: Objection — object to processing based on legitimate interest (art. 21).
policy.rightWithdraw: Withdrawal — take back your consent at any time, as easily as you gave it (art. 7(3)). This does not affect processing that was lawful before.
policy.rightComplaint: Complaint — lodge a complaint with your national data protection authority (art. 77).
policy.withdrawBody: Reopen the preferences at any time. Turning a category off stops it immediately; you can also erase the stored choice by clearing this site's data in your browser.
policy.currentChoice: Your current choice: analytics {{state}}, saved on {{date}}.
policy.noChoice: You have not made a choice yet — nothing optional is running.

privacy.title: How player data is processed
privacy.intro: SandStats records who played, against whom, and with what result, and publishes that as ratings and standings. This notice says what is collected, what is public, and what you can decide. It is written to meet the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
privacy.controllerBody: The controller is the operator of SandStats. For any question about your data, or to exercise the rights below, write to {{contact}}.
privacy.providedTitle: What you give us at sign-up
privacy.providedBody: Your email address, a password (stored only as a bcrypt hash — never in readable form), optionally your Telegram nickname, and the player you are: either an existing player you pick, or a new one you create with a name and a gender.
privacy.recordedTitle: What is recorded as you play
privacy.recordedBody: Every game you appear in: who your partner was, who you played against, the points, the date and the place. Which events you took part in and where you finished. Your registrations for tournaments, whether with a partner or alone — and, in a full-rotation tournament, which group you were in each round.
privacy.derivedBody: Your rating (an ELO-like number starting at 1000), the rating change and resulting rating after each individual game, your totals of games, wins and losses, your win rate, and your tournament medals.
privacy.publishedBody: SandStats is a public results site. Everything below is visible to anyone who opens it, without logging in, and is served by an API that requires no authentication:
privacy.publishedName: Your player name, or its masked form if you chose that (see below).
privacy.publishedRating: Your rating, its full history game by game, and your totals and win rate.
privacy.publishedResults: Every game you played, naming your partner and opponents, with the score.
privacy.publishedRegistrations: Which tournaments you are registered for, including while they are still open.
privacy.publishedWarning: This is the point of the site, and it is what you consent to when you register. Your email address and password are never published.
privacy.anonymityBody: You can ask us not to have your name shown in full — write to the address below. Every page of the site then renders it masked: "Artem Borzienkov" appears as "{{example}}", in leaderboards, results, standings and tournament rosters alike. You can ask us to turn this off again at any time.
privacy.anonymityLimitBody: Masking is applied when a name is displayed. Your real name stays in the database, is still returned by the public API, and is still visible to a tournament organiser who needs to tell players apart in order to record results. So it reduces how visibly your name is published — it is not technical anonymisation, and it does not make you unidentifiable. If you want your name removed rather than masked, use the erasure right below.
privacy.basisConsent: Publishing your name and your results rests on your consent (art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), given by ticking the box at sign-up; the moment you gave it is recorded. You can withdraw it at any time (art. 7(3)), which means asking us to remove your published data.
privacy.basisContract: Running your account and the tournaments you enter rests on the agreement between us (art. 6(1)(b)) and on legitimate interest in keeping a coherent competition record (art. 6(1)(f)) — a rating chain with games removed from the middle of it no longer describes anyone accurately.
privacy.recipientsBody: The site is hosted by a hosting provider acting as a processor, and anonymous usage measurement is provided by Vercel Inc. — only if you allowed it in the cookie banner. No data is sold, no advertising network is used, and no profiling beyond the sporting rating takes place. Where data is transferred outside the EEA it relies on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.
privacy.retentionBody: Your account is kept while it exists. Games and results are kept as part of the competition record, because removing one game changes every rating that followed it; on an erasure request we remove or de-identify your personal data and tell you what that means for the results you appear in.
privacy.exerciseBody: Write to {{contact}}. Tell us which player you are and what you want — a copy of your data, a correction, masking turned on or off, or erasure. You can also complain to your national data protection authority.
